title: Should Hyundai Bring This Blacked-Out Elantra N to the U.S.?

body_markdown:
Though we found few things to complain about when we drove the[Hyundai Elantra N](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/review-hyundais-elantra-n-is-feisty-fresh/) , we have to agree that the styling is not for everyone. Front-wheel-drive performance stalwarts like the[Honda Si](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/2025-honda-civic-si-all-grown-up-and-more-expensive/) or[Volkswagen GTI](https://www.hagerty.com/media/never-stop-driving/never-stop-driving-177-gti-review/) have long maintained an understated aesthetic, and Hyundai went with the exact opposite. The styling of the base Elantra is extroverted to begin with, full of creases and sharp edges, and we’d understand if the N variant with its spoiler and red accents (and pop-crackle exhaust) is simply too much for some.


Perhaps trying to tone things down a bit, Hyundai has introduced the Elantra N Monochrome. It celebrates the company’s performance brand, N, which has been around longer than you’d think and has won multiple Touring Car and World Rally Championship[titles](https://motorsport.hyundai.com/about-us/who-we-are) since its formation in 2012. The Elantra N nods to this lineage with a new forged wheel design in black and black Alcantara trim. That’s the Basic trim; you can upgrade to the Upper trim to get a carbon-fiber rear spoiler and mirror caps. The theme, as you might guess, is black.

The Monochrome edition is available in metallic black paint, with one other option: Performance Blue. This is the N-specific paint color and accent of choice in recent N products, so it’s only N-natural (ahem) that Hyundai would offer it on a model meant to celebrate N’s performance history. However, a Performance Blue Monochrome edition Elantra N is a bit of a misnomer, because the wheels and brake calipers are … black, not blue. Even so, we appreciate the spiderwebby wheel design and the carbon-fiber spoiler, and the Alcantara that wraps all the way around the steering wheel. On a Performance Blue car, the Monochrome edition becomes essentially a carbon-and-Alcantara accent pack. On an Abyss Black Pearl car, however, it is fairly ominous, and we like it. We’d complete the look with window tint as deep as the law would allow.


Hyundai


So, should Hyundai bring the Monochrome package to the U.S.? It sure makes sense to us: After all, last year North America was Hyundai’s best-performing market by sales volume. It’s competed in IMSA racing since 2019 and in the TC America series as far back as 2018, and as of 2025, it started a competition within that series exclusively for the Elantra N1 TC Evo. Plus, there’s[a strong tradition](https://www.hagerty.com/media/lists/black-friday-7-of-our-favorite-blacked-out-factory-models/) of black appearance packages here, from Ford to Dodge to Nissan. We’ve got reason to suspect that Hyundai is leaving the door ajar: The press release lists a planned launch in Korea, Canada, and Australia “with plans to expand to other global markets.”


If we might make a suggestion, Hyundai: Ditch the “Monochrome” title in favor of “N Heritage” or something and bundle all the goodies into a single trim with two colorways: Blacked-out, as above, or Performance Blue with white wheels to match the TCR car. Wouldn’t that be cool?
